To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ridership for rural, demand–response transit is positively related to the number of days of operation and the number of hours of operation per day.

total population and demographic characteristics are important factors for estimating ridership, fares have a negative effect, and providing additional days of service and allowing users to reserve their trips on shorter notice have a positive effect.

the number of trips taken on demand–response transit service is affected by the number of days that service is provided, the number of hours that service is provided each day, the number of days in advance that a trip can be requested, and the percentage of the local population that does not have access to a personal vehicle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of demand for rural public transit.
the estimation of demand–response transit ridership.
the development of a model for estimating demand–response transit ridership.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the models presented in this study are the best available models to date to estimate demand–response ridership.
a model for estimating rural demand–response ridership for the general public can be estimated using a combination of demographic and service variables.
the models developed here are useful tools that can be used by transit agencies to estimate the demand for demand–response transit service.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the models developed here provide a better understanding of factors affecting demand–response transit service ridership.
the model developed in this study can be used to estimate ridership for rural public demand–response services.
rural demand–response service is an important component of the rural transit network, and that it should be considered in planning and funding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
demand–response services can have a positive effect on the mobility of the population.
the characteristics of demand–response services and their geographic coverage have a significant influence on ridership.
the inclusion of specific service characteristics in the models improved model performance.
